stage_description: Young adulthood runs from maturity to about 3–4 years. The dog is physically mature but still developing behaviorally, with high energy and a strong need for mental work. This is the time to consolidate obedience, establish a stable routine, and build healthy habits that shape quality of life in the mature and senior years.
nutrition: Transition to a quality adult diet balanced for the breed's size, usually two meals a day. Portion and weight control matter: excess weight this early sets up joint and metabolic problems. Keep fresh water available at all times.
activity: Regular daily exercise — walks, play, agility, or running in a safe area. Mental enrichment (scent games, training) is as important as physical exercise and prevents boredom and destructive behavior.
veterinary_check_frequency: A routine exam once a year with scheduled booster vaccinations, weight checks, and parasite control. This is the baseline annual visit for a healthy adult dog and records normal values for future comparison.
dental_care: Daily or regular toothbrushing with dog-specific paste and plaque prevention. The veterinarian assesses the gums at the annual exam and recommends professional cleaning when needed.
warning_signs: Sharp changes in appetite or weight, reduced activity, limping, skin and coat problems, or changes in behavior or urination. Noticeable departures from the dog's normal state warrant a veterinary visit.
disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and does not replace consultation with a veterinarian.
